verifications.claim: NASA successfully launched the Artemis II mission on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT. (R1); The Artemis II crew blasted off on their lunar journey from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday. (R3); Artemis 2 LIVE: NASA Orion capsule unfurls solar wings (cited snippet)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the launch date and success on April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first crewed flight to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Their spectacular launch Wednesday evening marked the first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago. (R1); The last time astronauts traveled that far was Apollo 17, in December 1972. (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state it is the first crewed moon mission since Apollo era, over 50 years.

verifications.claim: The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket lifted off from Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The Artemis II mission is launching from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida, using the historic Launch Complex 39B. (R1); A towering orange-and-white NASA rocket blasted off from Florida... Kennedy Space Center (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of SLS launch from Kennedy Space Center.

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket sent four astronauts on a 10-day mission to orbit the Moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: four astronauts (R1); From launch... to splashdown on April 10, the mission is slated to last about nine and a half days. (R1); The Artemis crew will not land on the moon or even go into lunar orbit. Instead, the plan is to loop around it (R1); around the moon but not land there (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Four astronauts and ~10-day mission supported, but sources contradict 'orbit the Moon'—explicitly no lunar orbit, it's a flyby/loop.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests critical systems for future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: thoroughly test their Orion capsule... making sure the ship's communications, navigation, propulsion and life support systems are working properly before heading to the moon. (R1); Like Apollo 8, Artemis II aims to check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm testing systems for future missions including lunar landings.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a test flight, not a landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "It's a test flight" (R1); around the moon but not land there (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as test flight, no landing.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is aimed at validating life-support systems with a crew on board before future surface landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: check out all of (Orion's) environmental control, life support systems... before we press out to the moon (R1); Orion capsule, which is making only its second flight — and its first with a crew on board (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly validates life-support with crew for future missions.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission includes NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman (commander).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: commander Reid Wiseman (R1); Mr. Wiseman, the NASA astronaut who is the commander (R3)

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission to go beyond low Earth orbit since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Communications switch to Deep Space Network... first time in 50 years a spacecraft carrying people is traveling far enough (R1); first time humans reached another celestial body... last time astronauts traveled that far was Apollo 17, in December 1972 (R3)

verifications.claim: Artemis II features the first Black man to fly to the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Mr. Glover of NASA will be the first Black man to venture into deep space (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated for Glover in moon mission context.

verifications.claim: Artemis II features the first woman to fly to the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Ms. Koch of NASA will be the first woman to do so (R3)

verifications.claim: Artemis II features the first Canadian to fly to the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: first Canadian astronaut ever to travel beyond near-Earth orbit (R1); first person on a moon mission who is not an American (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly first Canadian beyond LEO/to moon.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft is designed to perform a 10-day trip.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: mission is slated to last about nine and a half days (R1); 10-day mission (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe ~10-day mission, but not explicitly 'designed to perform a 10-day trip'—broader mission context.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft's 10-day trip sets a record for the farthest distance traveled from Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: expected to set a record for the farthest distance humans have ever traveled from Earth: 252,000 miles (R1); set a distance record... 252,799 miles (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Directly states distance record during the mission.
